Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and helpful context on the search scenarios and content types. Quick recap + our recommended path for validating model fit for Lexicon's semantic search:

Summary of the call
- Core use case: retrieval-augmented search across product spec pages, support KB, and community forum threads (documents vary 200–5k tokens).
- Key quality priorities: strong recall for long-tail queries (rare terms), stable nearest-neighbor ordering for re-ranks, and tight false-positive control in top-5 results.
- Constraints: budget target for embeddings storage + query cost; latency SLO for web search < 120ms median.

Redwood recommendations (what we’ll validate)
1) redwood-emb-small-v2 (s512) — 512-dim, lowest cost, good for majority short-form queries; expected recall@10 ~0.78 on our generic eval.
2) redwood-emb-large-v1 (l1536-q4) — 1536-dim quantized variant, better separation for taxonomy-heavy content and long docs; expected recall@10 ~0.83–0.86 but ~2–3x storage/cost vs s512.

Why two candidates
- Start with s512 for a baseline and fast iteration. If we see long-tail drop-offs (low recall for product-specific terms), run the large variant and compare precision/recall curves and cluster separability.

Attached initial artifacts: lexicon_prompt_set_v1.csv (sample queries + canonical answers) and our internal eval summary pdf (lexicon_eval_report_v1.pdf). We can run a more representative job with the data you share.

Immediate next steps (mutual action plan)
- Lexicon: share a 1–2k sample of real documents (mix of KB, forum threads, specs). JSONL fine — please include doc_id, text, and a small set of query->gold doc mappings where available.
- Redwood: run a candidate eval across s512 and l1536-q4, return R-Precision, recall@10, MRR, and a simple drift/stability report. Link to eval run will be provided.
- Workshop: 60-min technical session to review results and pick a production path (suggest week of Oct 18).

- Any limits on embedding storage budget per million docs?

Connor / Alice / Ben —

Short technical notes on the points Alice raised and what we’ll produce in the eval:

1) Drift monitoring
- We track embedding drift with two complementary signals: (a) distributional shift on pairwise distances (we compute a monthly JS divergence on the distance histogram) and (b) top-k stability (fraction of query top-10 that remain identical between snapshots).
- Practical trigger: JS divergence increase > 0.12 OR top-10 stability < 0.75 for a 30-day window -> flag for re-embedding review. We’ll include a time-series plot in the report.

2) Dimensionality / quantization tradeoffs
- 512 vs 1536: 1536 typically improves MRR and recall for long documents and taxonomy-specific queries because more dimensions capture rare term semantics. Expect +3–7% absolute on recall@10 on these workloads.
- Quantization (we recommend 4-bit product quant, labeled l1536-q4): storage ~2.6–3.1x reduction vs float32 1536 with measured quality drop <2% on our bench for recall@10. Latency: raw NN query time increases slightly due to larger vectors unless you use IVF+PQ; for typical CPU/ANN infra the wall-clock difference is ~10–25ms for median query.

3) Suggested evaluation metrics (we will return these)
- recall@10, MRR, R-Precision, mean cosine similarity gap between true positive and nearest false positive, and top-10 stability over repeated samples.
- Also compute dimensionality diagnostics: PCA explained variance (top 10 components) and mean nearest-neighbor distance ratio (intra-cluster / inter-cluster).

4) Practical thresholds for Lexicon (recommendation)
- Production target: recall@10 >= 0.82, MRR >= 0.55. If s512 meets targets we recommend it for cost reasons; if not, l1536-q4 is the fallback.

5) Eval logistics
- We’ll run both candidates on the file you uploaded and post results to the eval run: https://app.redwood.ai/evals/run/ER-2026-1123 (will include plots and csv exports).
- Expected turn-around: 48–72 hours after we receive the cleaned sample.

If helpful, I’ll include a short script in the report that computes the JS divergence and top-k stability so your infra team can run it monthly.
